methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $66M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Chef Robotics, founded by Rajat Bhageria, is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $65.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparative universe of 9 peers (1 public, 8 private) spanning the same sector and adjacent development stages, including companies such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two primary valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $66M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to next-stage advancement, yielding $131M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B and a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. This method reflects the substantially higher valuations observed in the broader robotics cohort.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $112M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $916M across both methods. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around Chef Robotics' stage positioning relative to peers—most comparables are at Series B, one stage ahead. Key uncertainties include whether the company will achieve milestones supporting peer-level valuations, margin and revenue trajectory relative to the comparison set, and sector-wide robotics valuations. A narrower range of $300M–$800M may be warranted pending clarity on near-term commercial traction and competitive positioning.
